turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Hey David, I want to go over the discount code requirement before we start development.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Sure. Do we already know which customers should be able to use the code?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Yes. Logged-in customers can use it, but guest users shouldn't have access.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Okay. Has the client decided what happens if a guest tries to apply the code?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Yeah, they should see a message asking them to log in first.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Got it. Do we need to restrict the code to certain customer groups?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: For now, no. Any logged-in customer should be able to use it.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Okay. What should happen if the customer has already used another discount?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: They shouldn't be able to combine the discounts.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Makes sense. Should the system show an error message in that case?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Yes, and it should explain that only one discount can be used.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Okay. Have we confirmed whether the code needs to be validated before checkout?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Yes, the client wants it validated as soon as the customer applies it.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Got it. And if the code is expired, should we remove it automatically?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Yes. The discount should be removed and the customer should see a message.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Alright. I think that covers the main cases.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Great. I'll add these rules to the ticket so we're on the same page.
